v.rationale: All four implementations pass their suites and share the core design: onOneServer, a ShouldBeUnique job and retry_after raised above the job timeout. That makes the details decide the ranking. impl-2 is the most complete: every recurring task runs at a Copenhagen local time, the prune runs at 03:00 to avoid the spring-forward gap, it has a short withoutOverlapping lock and runInBackground, and its job attributes give Timeout < UniqueFor < 1h. Its tests cover DST due-ness, the 48h boundary, a real multi-batch prune and unique-lock expiry against a real queue. impl-3 is nearly identical but schedules the prune in UTC and has weaker test hygiene (unused imports, reflection, filler assertion). impl-1 is correct, with the leanest and most memory-efficient delete. Its older idioms (property signatures, inline query, Mail::raw) and thin tests (Symfony transport inspection, no DST or batch coverage) put it third. impl-4 has a real bug the task explicitly forbids, confirmed by a probe: UniqueFor(3600) equals the hourly interval, so a killed worker's lock causes the next hour to be skipped. Tries(3) without FailOnTimeout can re-run a 45-minute sync three times. It also adds an unrequested ConfirmableTrait/--force/--dry-run and has a sham 'several batches' test, so it ranks last.
